## TL;DR

The QA pass covered every Settings tab and the Agents page. It found and fixed a Notifications validation defect: a negative spend alert amount was silently discarded, and fractional amounts appeared allowed even though the server requires whole dollars. The field now provides inline, accessible validation and uses a whole-dollar step. A targeted regression test passes. A valid amount was also saved to an isolated scratch configuration and verified after browser reload.

## Work and rationale

The task’s first auth-less server run was served in preview mode, which intentionally rejects writes. The first attempt to test the spend threshold therefore did not establish persistence behavior. I kept that server’s safety boundary intact and used an in-process ephemeral server rooted at `.repoos/qa-1179-sandbox`, with a separate scratch `repoos.toml`. This provided a writable browser path without involving the worktree’s project configuration or any real RepoOS configuration.

On the scratch server, entering `12` saved `attention.spendAlertUsd = 12`; after reloading the browser page, the field still showed `12`. Entering `-1` returned the UI to the previous value without displaying why. Source inspection showed that the computed setter returned early for negative values, with no field error. The control’s `step="0.01"` also conflicted with server validation that accepts whole numbers.

The Settings view now keeps an explicit field error for invalid values. Negative amounts produce “Spend alert threshold must be zero or more.” Fractional values produce a whole-dollar message. The error is shown inline with `role="alert"`, the input exposes `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby`, and valid integer entry clears the error before saving. The step is now one dollar. I added the spend alert field to the Settings save test fixture and added a regression case that checks both invalid values do not trigger save, valid entry clears the error, and the valid value is sent to the config store.

The QA record documents the Settings tabs and Agents subpages visited, the observed agent/provider state, the isolated save/reload check, the defect, and the limits on what was exercised. No credentials, provider keys, task assignments, schedules, shared budget controls, or task state were modified.

## Approaches tried

I first used the required `just serve-noauth` flow from the task worktree. It correctly ran as a read-only preview child and blocked changes. I then used the repository’s in-process ephemeral server harness with an isolated scratch root to test a real config write and reload. I also attempted to use the browser automation host after rebuilding the UI; that host reported itself unavailable, so I relied on the component test for the post-fix inline validation behavior rather than claiming a second browser observation.

The direct Vitest invocation did not load the project’s Vue plugin configuration. I reran the test through the repository’s `bun run test` wrapper, which uses the configured UI test environment. Its first run revealed only an expectation mismatch: the config store sends number fields as strings. I corrected the test to assert the actual serialized config value (`"12"`) and reran successfully.

## Challenges and blockers

The preview server blocks all mutation requests, so it cannot prove save behavior. The isolated scratch server resolved that limitation without relaxing preview protections or touching the actual project `repoos.toml`. Browser automation was unavailable on the follow-up attempt, preventing visual confirmation of the new error in a rebuilt app. The regression test covers the exact interaction and accessible error state instead.

The visit was an inventory of the Settings and Agents pages, not a control-by-control mutation audit. Controls that would trigger external effects or require credentials were observed without being changed. The persistence check was representative rather than a claim that every setting was individually saved and reloaded.

## Key learnings

An input that silently ignores invalid values is a validation failure even when the stored value remains safe. The feedback needs to be adjacent to the control and tied to its accessibility state. The UI’s advertised precision should match the server’s accepted precision. For writable QA in this repository, an ephemeral test server with a dedicated scratch root is the safe way to verify persistence when the managed preview server is read-only.
